part.text:
Done — all 49 tests in `forth.spec.js` pass. The implementation lives entirely in `forth.js`:

- **Tokenizing**: `evaluate()` splits input on whitespace; numbers match `/^-?\d+$/` (handles negatives), everything else is a word, lowercased for case-insensitivity.
- **Builtins**: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (integer division via `Math.trunc`, with a "Division by zero" check), plus `dup`, `drop`, `swap`, `over`. Each pops the required operands and throws `Stack empty` when there aren't enough.
- **User words**: `: name ... ;` stores the definition in an instance map (so definitions are per-instance). The body is lowercased and any user words inside are expanded into their definitions at define-time — this makes `: bar foo ;` capture `foo`'s behavior as it existed when `bar` was defined, and lets `: foo foo 1 + ;` recurse through the previous definition. Defining a number as a name throws `Invalid definition`; unknown words at runtime throw `Unknown command`.

One subtlety worth noting: `dup` copies the top of the stack without removing it (`s.push(s[s.length - 1])`), and `-`/`/` pop the right operand first so `3 4 -` yields `-1` and `12 3 /` yields `4`.
